sentences.en: So that's after the Council of Constance, isn't it, where they get rid of the other three?

sentences.en: So at this point the Medici have become some of the richest people in Florence and Giovanni as a result of this becomes a big political player and he is elected

sentences.en: to the Signoria multiple times.

sentences.zh: 这是因为他备受尊敬，还是因为他在贿赂别人？

sentences.zh: 我觉得两者兼而有之吧。

sentences.en: I think he's genuinely respected and he's bribing people to an extent that we find it hard to discern through the sort of murk of history.
sentences.zh: 我认为他确实赢得了人们的真心尊敬，同时也进行了一定程度的贿赂，只是这种程度在历史的迷雾中很难被我们清晰地辨别出来。

sentences.en: Or offering patronage rather.
sentences.zh: 或者说提供的是庇护权。

sentences.en: Patronage yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，庇护。

sentences.en: It's not bribery to a scale that shocks people at the time.
sentences.zh: 这种规模的贿赂还没有达到在当时让人感到震惊的程度。

sentences.en: I think it's considered completely reasonable and far for the course.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这被认为完全合情合理，也是当时的常态。

sentences.en: So while all this is going on Cosimo is growing up in what's called the Casa Vecchia, which is the kind of stone Medici palace in the center of Florence.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这一切发生的同时，科西莫在被称为“旧宅”的建筑里长大，那是美第奇家族位于佛罗伦萨市中心的石头宅邸。

sentences.en: He goes to school as a nearby monastery.
sentences.zh: 他在附近的一所修道院上学。

sentences.en: He learns Latin, German, and French.
sentences.zh: 他学习拉丁语、德语和法语。

sentences.en: His tutor is a rich patrician called Roberto de Rossi, who is a classic humanist scholar.
sentences.zh: 他的家庭教师是一位名叫罗伯托·德·罗西的富有贵族，他是一位经典的文艺复兴人文主义学者。

sentences.en: And we should talk a little bit about humanism.
sentences.zh: 我们应该稍微聊聊人文主义。

sentences.en: So this is basically the study of the humanities, which means the study of the classical world.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是对人文学科的研究，也就是对古典世界的研究。

sentences.en: So it's grammar and rhetoric, but it's also philosophy and poetry and art, all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 所以它包括语法和修辞学，但也涵盖哲学、诗歌和艺术等等诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: And the very term humanism at this point, so when Cosimo is like 10, 12, 14, is really breaking through and becoming fashionable.
sentences.zh: 而在当时，也就是科西莫大约10岁、12岁、14岁的时候，“人文主义”这个词正在真正突破常规并变得流行起来。

sentences.en: And to become a humanist, in other words, to study Ovid and Plato and Aristotle and so on.
sentences.zh: 要成为一个崇尚人文主义的人，换句话说，就是要去研读奥维德、柏拉图、亚里士多德等等。

sentences.en: Well, not, I think, Plato at this point.
sentences.zh: 不过，我觉得当时还读不到柏拉图。

sentences.en: No, Plato is beginning to come through at this point, Tom.
sentences.zh: 不对，汤姆，柏拉图正是在这个时候开始逐渐进入人们的视野的。

sentences.en: Plato is really coming through in the 15th century.
sentences.zh: 柏拉图确实在15世纪开始受到重视。

sentences.en: Yeah, but there's the early signs of it at this point.
sentences.zh: 对，但当时已经有了早期的迹象。

sentences.en: And I think the important thing is that you need money, that humanism is a sign of status, because most of these humanist scholars work as private tutors.
sentences.zh: 我认为重要的一点是，你需要有钱，人文主义是身份地位的象征，因为这些人文主义学者大多作为私人教师工作。

sentences.en: They don't have institutional backing.
sentences.zh: 他们没有体制上的资金支持。

sentences.en: So in other words, you need to be able to afford a private tutor who will give you access to all of this kind of scholarship.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你需要支付得起一位私人家庭教师的费用，他能让你接触到所有这些学术知识。

sentences.en: And young Cosimo is exactly the kind of person who looks like to get into this.
sentences.zh: 而年轻的科西莫正是那种看起来很可能会涉足这一领域的人。

sentences.en: And actually, he really gets into it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他确实深深地沉浸其中。

sentences.en: So there's a great book and actually quite a caustic book about the Medici by Mary Hollingsworth.
sentences.zh: 有一本关于美第奇家族的极棒且文笔相当尖锐的书，作者是玛丽·霍林斯沃思。

sentences.en: And she points out that when he was in his late 20s, there was an inventory of his house.
sentences.zh: 她指出，当科西莫二十多岁接近三十岁时，曾有过一份他家中的藏书清单。

sentences.en: And the books were things like Cicero, Julius Caesar, Virgil, Marshall, Ovid, Tacitus.
sentences.zh: 上面的书包括西塞罗、尤利乌斯·恺撒、维吉尔、马提亚尔、奥维德、塔西佗。

sentences.en: And she says, you know, it's a big library for the period by any standards, but very unusual for somebody who's in their late 20s and is basically a banker, not a scholar.
sentences.zh: 她评价说，无论是按什么标准来看，对于那个时代来说这都是一个庞大的藏书库，而对于一个二十多岁、本质上是银行家而非学者的人来说，这就非常不寻常了。

sentences.en: And Dominic, can I just pick up on that list?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我能就那份书单说两句吗？

sentences.en: Tacitus, I mean, he has only just been discovered.
sentences.zh: 塔西佗，我是说，这本书当时才刚刚被重新发现。

sentences.en: So we know that Boccaccio, the great 14th century Florentine writer, is reading Tacitus, but nobody else really knows about him.
sentences.zh: 我们知道14世纪伟大的佛罗伦萨作家薄伽丘在读塔西佗，但除了他之外几乎没人知道这本书。

sentences.en: So for Cosimo to have Tacitus, he's amazingly cutting edge.
sentences.zh: 所以科西莫能拥有塔西佗的作品，说明他极其走在时代前沿。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of almost avant-garde in his tastes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他的品味几乎可以说是前卫的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 对，我也这么认为。

sentences.en: I think there's no underestimating all this or sort of underplaying it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得绝对不能低估所有这些，或者说不能对其轻描淡写。

sentences.en: I think clearly this is somebody who is really, really interested in all this and is keen to buy the latest things that have been discovered.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很显然，这个人对所有这一切都极其感兴趣，并且渴望买到最新发现的东西。

sentences.en: You know, keen to be at the sort of cutting edge.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，渴望走在某种潮流的前沿。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We don't get many glimpses of Cosimo as a young man.
sentences.zh: 我们很少能一窥科西莫年轻时的样子。

sentences.en: He seems to keep out of the public eye.
sentences.zh: 他似乎总是远离公众视线。

sentences.en: He's said to be very soberly dressed.
sentences.zh: 据说他的衣着非常朴素。

sentences.en: He doesn't go around with a big retinue.
sentences.zh: 他出行不带庞大的随从队伍。

sentences.en: He's said to have a kind of terse and sardonic sense of humour.
sentences.zh: 据说他有一种简练而讽刺的幽默感。

sentences.en: It's very Sambra.
sentences.zh: 这非常桑布拉。

sentences.en: I mean, now that you've said that, Tom, here's a definite point of difference.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，既然你已经这么说了，汤姆，这确实是一个明显的区别点。

sentences.en: He marries a woman called Contesina Dibadi, who's from another banking family.
sentences.zh: 他娶了一个名叫孔泰西娜·迪巴迪的女子，她来自另一个银行家族。

sentences.en: Christopher Hibbert describes her as fat, capable, and cheerful.
sentences.zh: 克里斯托弗·希伯特把她形容为身材发福、能干且性格开朗。

sentences.en: Certainly capable, and she's capable of being cheerful.
sentences.zh: 能干肯定是能干的，而且她也确实开朗。

sentences.en: But she's definitely not fat.
sentences.zh: 但她绝对不胖。

sentences.en: No, I just want to place that absolutely in the record.
sentences.zh: 不，我只是想把这一点明确记录在案。

sentences.en: And they have two children.
sentences.zh: 他们有两个孩子。

sentences.en: And he also, as you said earlier, he has this illegitimate son by one of his slave girls, a Circassian slave girl, a son called Carlo.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你刚才所说，他和他的一个女奴——一个切尔克斯女奴生了一个私生子，一个名叫卡洛的儿子。

sentences.en: This is absolutely standard, and he's brought up with his legitimate sons.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是标准操作，而且这个孩子是和他的嫡子们一起被抚养长大的。

sentences.en: He's trained as a banker from an early age.
sentences.zh: 他很小就开始接受银行家方面的培训。

sentences.en: His father sends him to branches in France and Germany.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲把他派往法国和德国的分支机构。

sentences.en: And then in 1420, Cosimo effectively takes over the family business.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1420年，科西莫实际上接管了家族企业。

sentences.en: Now, at this point, the Medici Bank is a really, really serious enterprise.
sentences.zh: 现在，在这个时候，美第奇银行已经是一个非常非常严肃的企业了。

sentences.en: It's one of the most sophisticated trade networks in Europe.
sentences.zh: 它是欧洲最复杂的贸易网络之一。

sentences.en: It's also a very sophisticated political network by this point.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，它也是一个非常复杂的政治网络。

sentences.en: He's got his cousin, Averado.
sentences.zh: 他有他的表弟阿韦拉多。

sentences.en: He's very good at running all this.
sentences.zh: 他非常擅长管理这一切。

sentences.en: And you asked, is it bribery?
sentences.zh: 你问过，这是行贿吗？

sentences.en: They're using loans, gifts, favors, all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他们使用贷款、礼物、人情，所有这些手段。

sentences.en: Offers people can't refuse.
sentences.zh: 人们无法拒绝的提议。

sentences.en: There is a mafia flavor to all this.
sentences.zh: 这一切带有一种黑手党的色彩。

sentences.en: They call their network their amici, their friends.
sentences.zh: 他们把自己的网络称为他们的amici，也就是他们的朋友。

sentences.en: And they don't refer to their friends.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不会直指他们的朋友。

sentences.en: When they're writing to each other, they will just say of somebody, he's a friend of ours, but they won't name him or go into details.
sentences.zh: 当他们通信时，提到某个人，他们只会说，他是我们的朋友，但绝不会说出他的名字或陷入细节。

sentences.en: So there is a sense, there's a slight shadiness.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种感觉，带有一点点见不得光的阴暗感。

sentences.en: And I mentioned Mary Hollingsworth's book.
sentences.zh: 我提到了玛丽·霍灵斯沃斯的书。

sentences.en: In her book, she points out that these are families who have migrated to Florence after the Black Death.
sentences.zh: 在她的书中，她指出这些家族都是在黑死病之后迁徙到佛罗伦萨的。

sentences.en: So they are newcomers.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是新来者。

sentences.en: They are self-made, aspirational families who are not part of the existing mercantile oligarchy.
sentences.zh: 他们是靠自己发家的、有抱负的家族，并不属于现有的商业寡头集团。

sentences.en: And these are people who perhaps feel a little bit snubbed and left out by the more conservative families.
sentences.zh: 这些人或许会觉得被那些更保守的家族有些冷落和排挤。

sentences.en: And so they are the people to whom the Medici are appealing.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们正是美第奇家族极力拉拢的对象。

sentences.en: And so there is a scope for someone who is fabulously wealthy to play the part of the friend of the people.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于一个极其富有的人来说，扮演人民之友的角色有着广阔的空间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we see it in ancient Rome and we see it in the modern American Republic.
sentences.zh: 我们在古罗马看到了这一点，在现代美利坚共和国也看到了这一点。

sentences.en: So maybe something that is inherent within the functioning of republics, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 所以这或许是共和国运作中固有的某种东西吧。

sentences.en: I think absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我想绝对是的。

sentences.en: There are so many parallels here with sort of the Roman Republic, I think, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我认为这与罗马共和国有太多相似之处了。

sentences.en: So Cosimo's father, Giovanni, dies in 1429.
sentences.zh: 所以科西莫的父亲乔瓦尼于1429年去世。

sentences.en: And there's some very famous words that are given to him on his deathbed.
sentences.zh: 他临终前留下了一些非常著名的遗言。

sentences.en: where Giovanni is meant to have said to Cosimo, be very wary about being summoned to the Palazzo della Signoria.
sentences.zh: 据说乔瓦尼曾对科西莫说，对于被传唤到领主宫（Palazzo della Signoria）一事，一定要非常警惕。

sentences.en: Wait to be summoned when you are summoned.
sentences.zh: 等到传唤你时再去。

sentences.en: Do as you ask.
sentences.zh: 做好你分内的事。

sentences.en: Never be conceited.
sentences.zh: 绝不要自负。

sentences.en: Never be proud.
sentences.zh: 绝不要傲慢。

sentences.en: Now, whether he actually said this, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 至于他是否真的说过这话，我们不得而知。

sentences.en: There's probably a kernel of truth in it, because I think it's clear at this point, the late 1420s, that the Medici's rivals are kind of sharpening their knives a bit.
sentences.zh: 其中可能包含着核心的真相，因为我认为到了这个时候，即1420年代末，美第奇家族的竞争对手们已经在磨刀霍霍了。

sentences.en: They're sick of the Medici.
sentences.zh: 他们受够了美第奇家族。

sentences.en: They're anxious about them, and they're ready to choose their moment to strike.
sentences.zh: 他们对美第奇感到焦虑，并准备挑选时机发起进攻。

sentences.en: and chief among them are this rival family that i mentioned before who are called the albizzi
sentences.zh: 其中最主要的，就是我之前提到过的那个名为阿尔比齐的对手家族。

sentences.zh: 阿尔比齐家族也是一个商人家族，不是贵族家族，他们的财富是通过羊毛和呢绒积累起来的。

sentences.en: wool from cloth but they have been major players from for longer than the medici they clearly

sentences.en: think no we want to get rid of these rivals before they become too big they haven't bought

sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。阿尔比齐家族继承了他们的家具，而美第奇家族则向艺术家定制各种华丽的家具。

sentences.en: commissioning kind of fancy furniture from from artists their leader is a guy called renaldo
sentences.zh: 他们的领袖是一个叫雷纳尔多的人。

sentences.en: and he is a kind of grizzled you know he'd be sean bean probably oh well that doesn't promise
sentences.zh: 他是一个饱经沧桑的人，你知道的，他大概长得就像肖恩·宾（Sean Bean）。哦，这对他的命运来说可不是什么好兆头。

sentences.en: well for his fate no exactly he's kind of grizzled he's a former soldier he's very haughty
sentences.zh: 不，一点没错，他饱经沧桑，曾是一名士兵，非常高傲，非常骄傲。

sentences.en: he's very proud and he says you know the medici absolute scum i can't stand the medici and he
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，美第奇家族简直就是群败类，我无法忍受美第奇家族。

sentences.en: actually gives a brilliant speech in 1426 his supporters which is reported in one of the
sentences.zh: 事实上，他在1426年向他的支持者发表了一场精彩的演讲，这被某部编年史记录了下来。

sentences.en: Chronicles.
sentences.zh: 编年史。
